#Handicapper
Why Are Handicappers Anonymous?

We track performance, not personalities.

Each handicapper receives a unique anonymous identifier. That consistent anonymous identity stays with the record, so the results can be followed over time without a public username.

How this works: TMR reads public pick threads and posts, records each selection with the time it was posted, and grades it after the game ends. A pick counts only if it was posted before the game started. Units assume 1 unit risked per pick at the posted price, or TMR’s reference price when a post gave none. A pick with neither counts in the record but not in units or ROI. Each handicapper is shown under a permanent alias and tracking number, never a username; the alias is assigned from the number and says nothing about the record. Outside handicappers, not TMR members. Past results do not predict future results.
